newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovnaft begins $526 mln upgrade project.
newsitem.headline: Slovnaft begins $526 mln upgrade project.

text.p: Slovak monopoly oil refiner Slovnaft a.s. on Monday began work on a $526 million residue upgrading project as part of a plan to make it one of Europe's leading oil processors.
In a ceremony laying the cornerstone for the upgrade, Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar noted the project was financed without government guarantees.

The main financing for the project came through a $250 million credit arranged by Citibank International, with $164 million coming from Slovnaft itself, and the remaining $112 million come from a 1995 Global Depositary Receipt (GDR) issue.

The project, named EFPA (Environmental Fuel Project Apollo) consists of a residue hydrocracking unit with a capacity of 1,200,000 tonnes a year (t/yr), a fluid catalytic cracking unit with 850,000 t/yr, a VGO hydrotreating unit with 1,000,000 t/yr, a sulphuric acid alkylation unit with 165,000 t/yr, a MTBE unit with 55,000 t/yr, a hydrogen production unit with 25,000 t/yr and two sulphur recovery units of 45,000 t/yr each.
The main contractors for the project are Chiyoda Corporation, Fluor Daniel, Mitsubishi, Honeywell, Stork E&C B.V., and Raytheon.
The internal rate of return (IRR) of EFPA, to be fully operational by 1999 is projected at 12.7 to 14.2 percent, payback time at 6.8 to 7.9 years.
The upgraded Slovnaft products will reduce the plant's sulphur emissions by 11,690 tonnes a year and sulphur emissions by consumers by an estimated 27,960 tonnes a year.
According to prelimimary figures Slovnaft's 1996 net profit totalled 1.29 billion crowns.
